title: Three complete projects, no connector.
intro: Penumbra, Apsis, and a network threat-hunting lab each own one question. They share evidence formats and case studies, not a separate integration layer.
principles: One sentence per project. If a module does not serve that sentence, it belongs somewhere else.
Every module produces evidence or a metric, not just code.
New work arrives as an optional module, not a rewrite of the core.
Projects cross-link through schemas and case studies, never through a connector repository.

projects.name: Penumbra
projects.thesis: Prove what a detection fired on, what happened next, and how well it performed.

modules.name: Detection library
modules.detail: 50 Sigma rules compiled to EQL and KQL, with ATT&CK coverage.

modules.name: Validation benchmark
modules.detail: 16 labelled windows across five indices; 6 TP, 0 FP, 1 FN.

modules.name: Threat hunting
modules.detail: Four hypothesis-driven hunts with queries, evidence, verdicts, and detection changes.

modules.name: IR casebook
modules.detail: Three structured close-outs with metrics, containment, eradication, recovery, communication, evidence, lessons, and open questions.

modules.name: Triage automation
modules.detail: Dry-run enrichment, incident grouping, playbook selection, and 78 recommended actions; no external API calls.

modules.name: Cloud detection pack
modules.detail: Three CloudTrail detections; two fired on the synthetic corpus, one is awaiting telemetry.

modules.name: Dashboard integration
modules.detail: Evidence workspace with four tabs, compact validation, expandable incidents, and interactive roadmap; further visual polish can follow.

projects.done: A reviewer can follow a hunt or a case from telemetry to verdict without reading the source code.

projects.name: Apsis
projects.thesis: Find every route from a low-privilege AWS principal to administrator, prove which ones are real, and sever them.

modules.name: IAM graph
modules.detail: Users, roles, policies, and every route to administrator.

modules.name: Minimum cut
modules.detail: The fewest permissions to revoke to close every route.

modules.name: Drift
modules.detail: Diff two account exports and fail a newly opened route.

modules.name: Observed paths
modules.detail: Overlay CloudTrail to mark theoretical and observed graph edges.

modules.name: Guardrails
modules.detail: Map each cut to an SCP, permission boundary, or AWS Config rule.

modules.name: Case study
modules.detail: A safe lab account or LocalStack path from low privilege to admin, with evidence and a verified fix.

projects.done: A reviewer can see a path, the evidence that it is real, and the guardrail that closes it.

projects.name: Network threat hunting
projects.thesis: Hunt C2, DNS tunneling, and lateral movement from packet capture to a defensible detection.

modules.name: Capture lab
modules.detail: Zeek and Suricata telemetry from approved public PCAPs.

modules.name: Hunt set
modules.detail: Five hypotheses: C2 beaconing, DNS tunneling, lateral movement, staging, and TLS or JA3.

modules.name: Detections
modules.detail: Five network detections with ATT&CK mapping and evidence.

modules.name: Reports
modules.detail: Two full hunt reports and one PCAP-to-detection walkthrough.

projects.done: A reviewer can replay a capture, see the hunt, and explain why the traffic is benign or malicious.

sequence: Finish Apsis: observed paths, guardrails, and the attack-path case study.
Penumbra extensions: hunting, IR casebook, triage automation, and the cloud pack are done; next is the dashboard integration pass.
Build the network threat-hunting lab after the two existing projects are complete.

shared.name: Alert schema
shared.detail: A common JSON shape for rule_id, technique, host, user, cloud, and evidence.

shared.name: Case template
shared.detail: Summary, timeline, evidence, verdict, containment, eradication, and lessons.

shared.name: Evidence manifest
shared.detail: Source, hash, timestamp, query, and retention note for every artifact.
